newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian inflation hits 27-year low, rate cut awaited.
newsitem.headline: Italian inflation hits 27-year low, rate cut awaited.

text.p: Italian inflation hit a 27-year low in November, according to figures published Thursday, fuelling hopes of a cut in interest rates before Christmas.
The national statistics office ISTAT said consumer price inflation last month was 2.6 percent year-on-year, down from 3 percent in October and 6 percent in November 1995.

Financial markets showed scant reaction as the data was in line with expectations, but dealers said the drop to levels not seen since June 1969, when the consumer price index was 2.5 percent, meant an interest rate cut was overdue.
Monthly inflation rose 0.3 percent in November, against 0.1 percent in October and 0.6 percent in November 1995, ISTAT said.

Annual inflation has fallen steadily since February and the downward trend should mean Prime Minister Romano Prodi is on track to meet his goal of average 1996 inflation of 3.9 percent, analysts said.
The Bank of Italy has pursued a tough policy against inflation, waiting 14 months, until July, before cutting the key discount rate, which sets the trend for commercial rates.
Further progress on inflation prompted a surprise second cut in October to 7.5 percent from 8.25.
Economists now expect the central bank to clip another half a percentage point off the rate by mid-December.
